recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一條遠比周圍細胞長的蛇形線蟲幼體（microfilaria），體內充滿密集排列的深紫色體核柱，一端逐漸變細，周圍有一圈透明空隙可能為鞘膜；鑑定為班氏絲蟲（Wuchereria bancrofti）需依鞘膜、頭間隙與尾端無末端核等細節。
features: Elongated, sinuous microfilaria many times longer than surrounding hematopoietic cells
Body filled with a column of closely packed, darkly staining somatic nuclei
Tapered end with nuclei not clearly extending to the tip
Clear space around the organism, possibly representing a sheath; fine sheath detail not resolved
Background marrow cells including lymphocytes, an eosinophilic granulocyte and erythroid precursors
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a long, sinuous microfilaria with a column of densely packed somatic nuclei and a tapered end, surrounded by a clear space that may represent a sheath. Background marrow elements, including lymphocytes, granulocytes and erythroid precursors, are present without Leishman-Donovan bodies in this field. Species-level features such as the cephalic space and tail nuclei cannot be reliably assessed at this magnification. Findings are consistent with microfilaremia; in this case the organism was identified as Wuchereria bancrofti, and a nocturnal thick blood film is recommended.

ddx.vs: Brugia microfilariae are sheathed but have a sheath staining pink with Giemsa and two separate terminal nuclei at the tail tip.
Loa loa is sheathed with nuclei extending continuously to the tip of the tail and shows diurnal periodicity.
Mansonella microfilariae are smaller, unsheathed and have a blunt tail with nuclei extending to the tip.
Fibrin strands lack an organized column of nuclei and defined head and tail ends.
